(a) **Unilateral and Bilateral Elements:**
- **Unilateral Element:** An element whose $V-I$ relationship depends on the direction of current or voltage (e.g., Diode, Transistor).
- **Bilateral Element:** An element whose characteristics are the same regardless of the direction of current flow (e.g., Resistor, Inductor, Capacitor).

(b) **Active and Passive Elements:**
- **Active Element:** An element capable of generating or delivering electrical energy to a circuit independently (e.g., Voltage source, Current source, Generator).
- **Passive Element:** An element that only consumes, absorbs, or stores energy without generating it (e.g., Resistor, Inductor, Capacitor).

(c) **Linear and Nonlinear Circuits:**
- **Linear Circuit:** A circuit where parameters (R, L, C) are constant and satisfy homogeneity and superposition principles.
- **Nonlinear Circuit:** A circuit containing at least one parameter whose value changes with voltage or current (e.g., Iron-core inductor, semiconductor diodes).

(d) **Junction and Loop:**
- **Junction:** A point in a circuit where three or more circuit branches meet.
- **Loop:** Any closed path in an electrical circuit where no node is encountered more than once in traversing the path.
